title: Content clipped when text spacing is increased
user_impact: Users who increase line/letter/word spacing for readability lose content.
technical_impact: Fixed height/width with overflow:hidden on text containers; measured before and after overriding the text spacing, only newly clipped text counts.
source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 Text Spacing; W3C text spacing bookmarklet technique
applicability: Rendered elements with text in the top document and its open shadow roots; only those with overflow: hidden can clip.
expectation:
Review (not a violation) when applying the 1.4.12 minimums (line height 1.5,
paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em) makes a
container clip text it did not clip before (Rendering::text_spacing_clip, a
before/after pair measured by accessibility::probes): a fixed-height badge
(20px at line-height 1.2) or a fixed-width, nowrap label. Content clipped
already before the change (teasers cut by design, the 1x1 visually-hidden
pattern) is not caused by spacing and not reported. A container exactly as
tall as one line at 1.5 (24px) still fits; one that grows (min-height) or
whose fixed height a script removes after load passes. Every newly clipped
element is reported. The override is a constructed stylesheet adopted through
the CSSOM, so a CSP style-src does not block it (visual_text_spacing_csp).
Where the override does not reach the element (the page wins with a stronger
!important), nothing was measured: the rule is recorded as not run
(CapabilityMissing), never as a pass (visual_text_spacing_override_defeated).
